title: Lesson 23. Project and presentation talk
description: Finish the presentation with a checklist, rehearse and present

questions.prompt: Build the start of the talk
questions.explain: Greet, introduce yourself, name the topic.

questions.prompt: How many slides should the project have?
While presenting we speak loudly and stand straight.
questions.explain: Then everyone hears and sees you.

questions.prompt: Match the checklist item with an example

questions.explain: The slide helps; you do the telling.

questions.text: At the end we say: "Thank you for ___!"

questions.prompt: After the talk the audience can ask a question.
If parents can't come, what do we do?
options: Record a video and send it
questions.explain: The video shows them the talk.

learn.intro: Today you're a real speaker! We finish the presentation and present it to an audience.

slides.text: Check: a cover with the topic and name; 4–6 slides; a title and picture on each; little text; the last slide says "Thank you for listening!".

check.prompt: What goes on the last slide?

slides.text: A real speaker **doesn't read from the slide** — they tell it, and the slide helps. 1–2 sentences of your own per slide.
Stand straight, speak loudly, look at the audience. Start: "Hello! My name is… My topic is…". End: "Thank you for listening!"

check.prompt: A good speaker reads all the text off the slide.
check.explain: We tell it in our own words.

slides.text: Present to parents (or record a video). After that, the audience asks a question like real listeners.

check.prompt: Where do you look while presenting?
check.explain: At the audience, not just the screen.
